summary: Only Farmer's Walk has real 5-level percentile standards in the app's own scheme: Strength Level (lifter population, 20 m, per hand) with bodyweight ratios per hand - men 0.10/0.25/0.45/0.70/1.05x, women 0.05/0.15/0.30/0.50/0.75x (medium confidence; small sample, especially female). Kettlebell Farmer's Carry can reuse these; Suitcase Carry could reuse them with an assumed discount. Dead Hang has no validated population percentiles: only fitness-site tiers (e.g. 10-20/21-45/46-90/>90 s), Attia targets (120 s men / 90 s women at 40+), and one small study (active young adults: men 64+/-35 s, women 48+/-29 s) - rankable with low-medium confidence, time-based and not bodyweight-dependent. Plate Pinch has solid clinical pinch-gauge norms (Mathiowetz 1985, high confidence) but they do not convert to plate load; plate anchors (2x45 lb = very advanced/world class for men) are anecdotal - low. Hand Gripper: CoC ratings are exact, but population share is only qualitative (No.1 stops most lifters, No.3 elite) - low. Wrist curl/dumbbell wrist curl Strength Level standards exist but look noisy; finger curls have no data - low. Towel Hang, Towel Pull-Up, Fat Grip Hold, Static Barbell Hold, Plate Pinch Carry: no standards found; only anecdotes or proxies (pull-up standards). Grip dynamometer norms (NHANES peak combined 216.4/136.5 lb; Dodds peak median 51/31 kg; Topend rating bands) are high-quality and could act as a bridge if the app ever estimates grip strength, but percentile tables were not visible in snippets.
